rv.q: The well-sung show bops along at a good pace, cocktails flowed from busy, white-coated bartenders at intermission, and hoops and hollers flowed just as consistently from a Southport Corridor audience out for some PG-13 fun.
“Young Frankenstein” is a seasonally fitting giggle fest wrought with cheesy double-entendres and monstrous puns.
“Young Frankenstein,” a live stage musical version of Mel Brooks hysterical 1974 comedy film, is an absolute hoot in its new production at Chicago’s intimate Mercury Theatre on Southport.
Mercury Theater has recreated that magic with a cast and ensemble of top musical actors.
This demonically driving production of “Young Frankenstein” is one of Mercury Theater’s finest, to date.
I’ve always been a huge Mel Brooks fan but that’s not a requirement to enjoy this stellar laugh-out-loud night of frivolity that’s playing through December 31.
Roth steals the show with her give-it-all performance of 'He Vas My Boyfriend,' leaving nothing on the stage.

That reworked West End version of Young Frankenstein is getting its Chicago premiere in a spirited Mercury Theater production that will delight fans of the film even as the material still struggles to reach the comedic heights of The Producers.
Whether you are a fan of Brooks' movies or just like a good time, you'll find an enjoyable evening out in this show.

This two-act, 19 songs, 2 hours 30 minutes, including one 15-minute intermission production of Young Frankenstein, is another example of Mercury Theater's combination of choosing outstanding plays and an exceptional cast, making it a worthy Brooks comedy.
This is one that you might want to see several times.
Mercury’s Young Frankenstein is wild, wacky, and absolutely hilarious.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this Mercury Theater production of "Young Frankenstein," praising its hilarious performances, excellent musical numbers, and skillful staging that brings Mel Brooks' beloved comedy to vibrant life on an intimate stage.
